front.title: MAP Trust: Execution Receipts, Evidence Exchange, and Local Reputation

abstract.t: Defines the evidence layer of MAP: dual-signed ExecutionReceipts as immutable facts of past interactions, selective (pull-based) evidence disclosure, admission-cost mechanisms that make identities non-free where meshes require it, graduated trust bootstrap for new agents, informative guidance for computing local trust from evidence, and audit mechanisms (canary challenges, redundant execution, promise-vs-observation checks). No global reputation exists in MAP; this document standardizes evidence, not scores.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document family are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here. No adaptation or weakening of these terms applies.

section.name: Model and prohibitions
section.t: Trust in MAP is a local, derived projection over signed facts:

ul.li: P1: Descriptors, status reports, quotes, and any other self-issued

section.t: object MUST NOT carry trust, reputation, hallucination-rate, or tasks-completed fields. Self-attestation of trustworthiness is meaningless and was the central defect of the source designs (critique C1). Public-mesh policy SHOULD treat violations as non-conformant descriptors.

ul.li: P2: The only protocol-defined trust inputs are: ExecutionReceipts (§3),

section.t: challenge outcomes (§8), promise-vs-observation deltas the evaluator measured itself (quoted TTFT vs. receipt TTFT), and vouch records (§5.3).

ul.li: P3: How an agent turns evidence into decisions is local policy (§7 is

section.t: informative). Two conformant agents may disagree about a third — by design (arch T4).

Data semantics (normative): a receipt is a domain event — a past-tense fact, immutable once dual-signed, identified by its content address. Receipt stores are append-only; ingestion MUST be idempotent (dedup by content address) and replay-safe. Trust scores are derived data and MUST be rebuildable from the receipt store alone; implementations MUST NOT treat a cached score as authoritative over its evidence. Ordering across receipts is by their signed timestamps within each (peer, capability) scope; no global order exists or is needed.

section.name: Receipt lifecycle
section.sourcecode: Requester Provider | verify COMPLETE transcript-root (tasks §4) | | build ReceiptCore; sign role 1 | | -- RECEIPT {core, sig_req} ---------------→ | verify core against own | | records; sign role 2 | ←-- RECEIPT_ACK {full dual Receipt} ------- | store; done | store dual-signed receipt |
section.t: RECEIPT_ACK content is the COMPLETE dual-signed Receipt {1: core, 2: sig_req, 3: sig_prov} — not the provider signature alone — so the requester stores it without reassembly. A provider that refuses to countersign because the claimed usage/timestamps fall outside its countersignature tolerance (§3) replies ERROR 2006 (countersignature refused, core §9), retryable = false.

Either party MAY hold a receipt; both SHOULD. The provider's incentive to countersign is direct: dual-signed receipts are its portable, verifiable track record. A provider MAY refuse to countersign (e.g., it disputes a rating); the requester then holds a unilateral receipt — still valid evidence, but consumers weight it as an assertion of the issuer alone (§7). Requesters likewise SHOULD issue receipts for failures and timeouts (outcomes 1–3): honest negative evidence is what makes the system informative. A provider that only ever countersigns successes reveals that pattern in the gap between its receipt density and its quote volume — itself a signal.

section.name: ExecutionReceipt (wire format)
section.t: Matches test vector TV-002 byte-for-byte.
section.sourcecode:
Receipt = { 1 => bstr .cbor ReceiptCore, ; exact signed bytes — core I1 applies ? 2 => bstr .size 64, ; sig_req = Sign(enc(["MAPReceipt", 1, core-bytes])) ? 3 => bstr .size 64 ; sig_prov = Sign(enc(["MAPReceipt", 2, core-bytes])) } ; at least one of 2,3 present
ReceiptCore = { 1 => TaskID, ; also binds tasks §1 idempotency key 2 => AgentID, ; requester 3 => AgentID, ; provider 4 => CapURI, 5 => Timestamp, ; started 6 => Timestamp, ; ended 7 => uint, ; outcome: 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 timeout, ; 3 cancelled, 4 disputed 8 => { 1 => uint, 2 => uint, ; tokens-in, tokens-out, 3 => uint, 4 => uint }, ; ttft-ms, wall-ms (as observed by signer ; of role 1; provider countersignature ; attests agreement within tolerance) ? 9 => uint .le 100, ; rating — explicitly a subjective ; assertion, never "verified" ? 10 => bstr, ; payment reference (pay §5) ? 11 => Multihash ; transcript-root (tasks §8.1) }
section.t: Validation: both signatures verify over the received core bytes with the role-tagged structure shown (roles prevent signature confusion between parties); 2/3 identities MUST match core fields 2/3 or chain to them via delegation (identity §4); timestamps sane (5 ≤ 6, within object freshness policy). The transcript-root links the receipt to the concrete output commitment, so a receipt can anchor a dispute or an audit without disclosing the output itself.

Countersignature agreement tolerance (assigned 2026-07-06 from TASK-008; the numeric window trust §3 previously left open). A provider countersigns only if the requester's claimed core matches its own observation: task-id, capability, and identities (fields 1–4) MUST be exactly equal, and each usage field (8.1–8.4) MUST be within ±5% of the provider's OBSERVED value (minimum ±1), with started/ ended timestamps (5,6) within ±2000 ms. The tolerance band is anchored to the observed (provider, trusted) value, NOT max(claimed, observed), so an inflated claim cannot widen its own acceptance band — this is the countersignature-farming defense (§11). A mismatch → the provider replies ERROR 2006 (countersignature refused, core §9, retryable = false) and does not countersign; the requester keeps a unilateral receipt.

Outcome mapping (field 7) from the requester's task terminal (tasks §13): a Verified completion → 0 (ok); a Failed task → 1 (failed); a TTFT-timeout CANCEL (tasks §2, error 5001) → 3 (cancelled). Codes 2 (timeout) and 4 (disputed) are set by other paths and are not requester-task-terminal:

ul.li: Code 2 (timeout) is produced by a provider-side deadline miss — the

section.t: provider lets the task's deadline (tasks §82) elapse without a COMPLETE; this is reported on the requester side as error 5001 (TTFT miss, tasks §105/§454) and recorded as a receipt with outcome 2. It is distinct from the requester-terminal CANCEL (outcome 3).

ul.li: Code 4 (disputed) is produced by the dispute protocol (pay §6); a

section.t: receipt with outcome 4 records the event on the trust plane (pay §638).

This ExecutionReceipt field-7 outcome vocabulary (0 ok, 1 failed, 2 timeout, 3 cancelled, 4 disputed) is separate from the Complete message's own outcome field (tasks §181: 0 ok, 1 partial, 2 failed), which describes the task result carried in the COMPLETE message, not the receipt outcome. The two numeric scales overlap by coincidence; they are different structures and MUST NOT be conflated.

section.name: Evidence exchange — selective disclosure
section.t: Global receipt gossip is NOT RECOMMENDED (it publishes a who-computed- what-for-whom social graph; critique). Evidence moves by pull:
section.sourcecode: EvidenceQuery = { ; msg-type 0x0302 1 => AgentID, ; subject ? 2 => CapURI, ; scope ? 3 => [Timestamp, Timestamp], ; window ? 4 => uint, ; limit (default 64) ? 5 => uint ; role filter: 1 as-provider, 2 as-requester } EvidenceSet = { ; msg-type 0x0303; flows under FLOW_CREDIT 1 => [* Receipt], ? 2 => bool ; more available }
section.t: Any holder MAY answer for any subject — typically you ask a candidate provider for its own receipts, then discount by your trust in each receipt's requester-signer. Holders choose their audiences (a receipt is the holder's data; disclosure is voluntary), MAY redact field 9 or supply rating-blinded variants, and MUST NOT alter signed bytes (redaction = omission of the optional field only where a re-signed blinded core was produced at issuance time as a paired variant; otherwise disclose whole or not at all). Consumers MUST verify every receipt independently — evidence sets are untrusted transport, like the DHT.

section.name: Admission costs (Sybil economics)
section.t: Identity creation is free by default (arch T3); meshes that need scarcity choose one or more, declared in mesh policy and checked at descriptor ingestion or first contact:

section.name: Proof-of-work join tickets
section.t: JoinTicket = {AgentID, mesh-id, epoch, nonce} such that H(ticket) < target; epoch-bound (default 30 days) so tickets expire and grinding cannot be amortized forever. Equalizes nothing between a laptop and a datacenter — stated plainly — but raises mass-identity cost by orders of magnitude. A VDF variant substitutes sequential time for parallel hashing where hardware asymmetry matters.

section.name: Stake attestations
section.t: An opaque, settlement-method-scoped proof that value is locked and slashable under that method's rules (e.g., a bonded Lightning channel, an escrowed deposit). MAP carries the attestation (ExtMap of the descriptor) and defines nothing about custody or slashing — those belong to the settlement method (pay §5), avoiding the undefined "smart-contract- like ledger" of the source designs (critique C15/C9).

section.name: Social vouching
section.t: A vouch is a DelegationCert-shaped record: issuer attests "I vouch for subject up to scope S until T". Vouches are evidence weighted by the evaluator's trust in the voucher, and transitively discounted like any opinion (§7.3). A Sybil army vouched only by itself carries zero weight for anyone outside the ring — the structural containment that makes per-observer trust Sybil-aware.

section.name: Residual risk (honest statement)
section.t: No decentralized mechanism eliminates Sybil attacks; MAP's defense is layered cost plus the fact that fresh identities hold no evidence anyone weights. What admission costs buy is a floor price on attack scale, and what local trust buys is that reputation cannot be transferred into or out of a Sybil ring. Claims beyond this are not made (contrast critique C15).

section.name: Graduated bootstrap
section.t: New agents (zero evidence) are not excluded; they are priced in risk:

ul.li: Tier 0 (no evidence): eligible for canary/low-stakes tasks, small

section.t: contexts, escrowed or postpaid terms; requesters SHOULD cap concurrent exposure.

ul.li: Tier 1 (evidence exists, low confidence): normal tasks with tightened

section.t: TTFT/deadline enforcement.

ul.li: Tier 2 (high confidence for a capability): full eligibility per local

section.t: policy. Tiers are local policy vocabulary, not protocol state; they appear here so implementations converge on interoperable behavior (a mesh where nobody routes to the unproven never grows — design3's bootstrap observation, adopted).

section.name: Computing trust locally (informative)
section.t: Recommended default — Beta reputation per (subject, capability):
section.sourcecode: For each verified receipt r about subject s, capability c: w(r) = trust_in_issuer(r) × decay(now − r.ended) ; decay λ ≈ 0.98/day outcome 0 → α += w(r); outcomes 1,2 → β += w(r) (outcome 3 cancelled: ignore unless pattern; 4: β += 2w pending dispute) score(s,c) = α / (α + β) ; with prior α₀ = β₀ = 1 confidence(s,c) = α + β
section.t: Gate high-value routing on confidence ≥ floor, not score alone. Transitive opinions (peers' evidence summaries) are discounted by your trust in the peer and capped at 2 hops; EigenTrust-style global iteration is compatible but OPTIONAL and never on the routing critical path (arch §9). Promise-vs-observation deltas (quoted vs. receipt TTFT; claimed vs. verified transcript root) SHOULD feed the same α/β as strong signals. Rebuild rule (normative even though the formula is not): whatever function you choose, recomputing it from the receipt store MUST reproduce your scores — no write path MAY update a score without its evidence.

section.name: Challenges and audits
section.t: requester submits a task with a privately known reference answer, indistinguishable on the wire from real work; grading is local. Format: Challenge = ordinary ASSIGN; the message types exist for disclosed challenges used in mesh-level audit programs where providers opt in for a trust lift.

ul.li: Redundant execution: dispatch the same task to k providers, compare

section.t: transcript roots or graded outputs; disagreement lowers all, agreement raises all — collusion-resistant when the k-set is sampled from disjoint trust neighborhoods.

ul.li: Attestation lift: TEE-attested SecurityProfile raises priors only;

section.t: it never substitutes for evidence (attestation proves the stack, not the behavior).

tr.td: Issuer-trust weighting: receipts signed by unknowns carry ~0 weight (§7)
Weight flows only along the evaluator's own trust edges; rings are internally dense, externally weightless; redundant-execution sampling across neighborhoods detects output fraud
Unilateral receipts weighted by trust in issuer; provider's countersigned corpus dominates
Evidence non-transferable; admission cost (§5) re-paid; Tier-0 exposure caps bound damage
Rate limits (core §8.3), storage quotas, payment-linkage preference (receipts referencing settled invoices weight higher)
Requester-held unilateral negatives still circulate; density-vs-volume gap is itself evidence (§2)

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Receipts are pseudonymous personal data in some jurisdictions — retention and disclosure are holder decisions; the protocol never compels publication (compliance notes: ops §9). Rating (field 9) is subjective by declaration; UIs MUST NOT present it as verified. Evidence pulls reveal who is evaluating whom; route via relay where that matters (discovery §9). The dominant residual risk is correlated model failure masquerading as collusion (k providers running the same wrong model agree); mitigate by diversifying ModelEntry.weights-digest across the redundant set.

section.name: IANA-Style Considerations
section.t: Registers: receipt outcome codes; evidence query parameters; vouch caveat keys; challenge disclosure modes. The assigned values and the family-wide index are in draft-map-wire-01.md §3.16 and §3.17; in case of divergence the normative definitions in §3 and §8 govern.
